# Import Finished Work Into Git

Work is built to completion outside version control, then imported in a burst. Git holds the
**artefact**, not the **process**. Confirmed in 11 of 15 source repositories, contradicted in two,
and split in one — which makes it the single strongest signal about how this developer works.

## The shape

| Repo | Commits | Span | Tell |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence` | 7 | **4 seconds** | 12:17:39 → 12:17:43 |
| `labour-fraud-analysis` | 8 | **1 second** (7 of 8) | 16:19:26 → 16:19:27 |
| `Oracle-Database-Laboratories` | 8 | **3 seconds** | 12:16:30 → 12:16:33 |
| `Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories` | 5 | **3 seconds** | 12:18:09 → 12:18:12 |
| `IT Applications in Business and Commerce` | 8 of 11 | **6 seconds** | 20:46:11 → 20:46:17 |
| `Information-Systems-Modelling` | 3 | **10 seconds** | labs 1–3, 8,013 insertions |
| `Python-Programming-Laboratories` | 12 | one day | tests committed *before* the code they test |
| `browser_game_stickfps` | 9 | ~7 hours | ten days of mtimes, ordered by topic not chronology |
| `Farley` | 12 | two bursts | first commit alone = 172 files / 22,151 insertions |

Single commits carrying whole finished systems: `Information-Systems-Modelling` `aca049c` at **274
files / 39,273 insertions**; `Optimization Methods` `final_project` at **224 files / 17,075
insertions**; `Farley` `ff41677` at **172 files / 22,151 insertions**.

## Why this matters to the wiki

The real working log lives somewhere else, and it is richer than git:

- `browser_game_stickfps/PROGRESS.md` — 40.5 KB, eleven post-launch rounds, every dead end
- `Farley/docs/ocr-overlay/CHANGELOG.md` — dated entries for 2026-07-02/03 that **predate the repo**
- `IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/` — 846 lines auditing a
  *different* repository's eight branches
- `Optimization Methods/final_project/docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md` — "Date of check: 2026-07-09"

Commit messages describe artefacts ("Add the React Three Fiber game client"), never work. So the
`session` layer and these in-repo logs are the only records of *why* — see
[[progress-md-as-build-log]] and [[branch-per-experiment]].

## What the bursts actually were

Not a portfolio push and not a submission deadline:

> "Just cleaning up local folders."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

The clustering on 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-25 is **consolidation**, incidental to any external event.
Earlier drafts of this analysis read the batching as release events; the interview corrected that.
Git here is a *storage* channel, distinct from the *publishing* step in
[[presentation-polish-tail-commits]].

## The counter-examples

Two repos genuinely contradict the pattern, and both are course-long:

- **`Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories`** — 49 commits, 2026-03-20 → 07-10, five working dates with
  real gaps, and commits that exist only because something broke: `48ba16d Fix UnicodeEncodeError in
  the lab3 demos on Windows consoles`, `06b5882 Make SentinelNet run offline: vendor React,
  precompile the JSX`, `8a2acfe … stop tracking compiled bytecode`.
- **`Optimization Methods`** — 69 commits over 105 days, author date == commit date throughout,
  four cross-machine merges, and a traceable mid-stream fix (`d72e8bf fixed no run on tabu search on
  high talliard instances`). **Split verdict:** `first_project` is a real working log;
  `final_project` and `exam_prep` arrived as single squashed commits after an 81-day silence.

Even in the contradicting repos, *within-session* granularity stays upload-shaped — nine lab-3 files
each in their own commit, message equal to the file path; one commit is literally
`Add files via upload` from the GitHub web UI.

## Caveat on the survey

`brain.py survey` reported `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` as first = last = 2026-07-10, hiding a
four-month history. **The survey's git dates are unreliable**; every date on the wiki pages was taken
from `git log` directly.
